verdict.rationale: Consensus's core interaction model is natural-language search/synthesis (an 'AI-native alternative to Google Scholar' that lets you ask questions and get cited answers), and its 'research agent' chains citation crawling, DOI lookup, and similar-paper search automatically on top of a query. This shows NL-driven operation and some agentic chaining, but there's no evidence of broader NL 'commands' for managing the product (e.g., library actions, exports, settings) beyond search/synthesis queries. Missing for 10: evidence of NL commands controlling non-search actions (library management, workflow automation beyond search), and independent/hands-on corroboration of the research-agent's command-following behavior.
